label: suspect

unstated.what: When a CSV file cannot be opened, the command's stderr must contain the literal relative file path (e.g. 'styles/fixtures/default_names.csv' or 'styles/locale/cs/names.csv'); instruction only says the command must fail
unstated.quote: grep -q "styles/fixtures/default_names.csv" err || fail "F2 stderr: $(cat err)" / grep -q "styles/locale/cs/names.csv" err

unstated.what: When a required CSV column is missing, the command's stderr must contain the literal missing column name ('slug' for default_names.csv, 'name_cs' for names.csv); instruction never mentions error message content
unstated.quote: grep -q "slug" err || fail "F4 stderr: $(cat err)" / grep -q "name_cs" err || fail "F5 stderr: $(cat err)"

unstated.what: The unknown-slug warning written to stderr must include the offending slug value ('unknown-slug'); instruction only says 'logged as a warning'
unstated.quote: grep -q 'unknown-slug' err || fail "F1 missing unknown-slug warning: $(cat err)"

unstated.what: Paths are resolved relative to the current working directory (case dirs contain styles/..., not the repo), i.e. 'styles/fixtures/default_names.csv' and 'styles/locale/<lang>/names.csv' must be opened from cwd, not from a package/app directory

instruction_covers: management command name load_default_names with no required flags
default_names.csv columns slug,group,order,name_en and update/create semantics with blank-field skipping
per-language locale names.csv update flow, skipping LANGUAGE_CODE, blank translations ignored
unknown slug in translation CSV must not create a row
exit code 0 on success; non-zero exit when a CSV is missing, unopenable, or lacks a required column
reason: The functional behavior (exit codes, DB results, no row for unknown slug) is covered by the instruction, but the tests additionally grep stderr for exact diagnostics: file paths and missing column names on failures, and the offending slug in the unknown-slug warning, none of which the instruction specifies. Path resolution relative to cwd is also assumed but is the natural reading of the stated paths.
